audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Timothy text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for overseers, servants/deacons, women/wives ambiguity, household conduct, mystery of godliness.

verses.restored: Trustworthy is the saying: if anyone reaches toward oversight, one desires a beautiful/good work.

familiar.text: This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

modern.text: This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.

original.text: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος· εἴ τις ἐπισκοπῆς ὀρέγεται, καλοῦ ἔργου ἐπιθυμεῖ.

verses.restored: Therefore the overseer must be above reproach, husband of one wife, sober, sound-minded, respectable, hospitable, skilled in teaching,

familiar.text: A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach;

modern.text: An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,

original.text: δεῖ οὖν τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνεπίλημπτον εἶναι, μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρα, νηφάλιον, σώφρονα, κόσμιον, φιλόξενον, διδακτικόν,

verses.restored: not given to wine, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not lover of silver,

familiar.text: Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;

modern.text: not dependent on wine, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and free of the love of money.

original.text: μὴ πάροινον, μὴ ⸀πλήκτην, ἀλλὰ ἐπιεικῆ, ἄμαχον, ἀφιλάργυρον,

verses.restored: leading one's own household beautifully/well, having children in submission with all dignity,

familiar.text: One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity;

modern.text: An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.

original.text: τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου καλῶς προϊστάμενον, τέκνα ἔχοντα ἐν ὑποταγῇ μετὰ πάσης σεμνότητος·

verses.restored: but if someone does not know how to lead one's own household, how will one care for the assembly of the Divine?

familiar.text: (For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)

modern.text: For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church of God?

original.text: (εἰ δέ τις τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου προστῆναι οὐκ οἶδεν, πῶς ἐκκλησίας θεοῦ ἐπιμελήσεται;)

verses.restored: not newly planted, lest being puffed up one fall into judgment of the adversarial one.

familiar.text: Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

modern.text: He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil.

original.text: μὴ νεόφυτον, ἵνα μὴ τυφωθεὶς εἰς κρίμα ἐμπέσῃ τοῦ διαβόλου.

verses.restored: But it is also necessary to have a beautiful/good witness from those outside, so that one may not fall into reproach and snare of the adversarial one.

familiar.text: Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

modern.text: Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil. Qualifications for Deacons (Acts 6:1–7)

original.text: δεῖ ⸀δὲ καὶ μαρτυρίαν καλὴν ἔχειν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔξωθεν, ἵνα μὴ εἰς ὀνειδισμὸν ἐμπέσῃ καὶ παγίδα τοῦ διαβόλου.

verses.restored: Servants/deacons likewise: dignified, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy for shameful gain,

familiar.text: Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;

modern.text: Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued or given to much wine or greedy for money.

original.text: Διακόνους ὡσαύτως σεμνούς, μὴ διλόγους, μὴ οἴνῳ πολλῷ προσέχοντας, μὴ αἰσχροκερδεῖς,

verses.restored: holding the mystery of the trust in a pure conscience.

familiar.text: Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.

modern.text: They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.

original.text: ἔχοντας τὸ μυστήριον τῆς πίστεως ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει.

verses.restored: And let these also be tested first; then let them serve if they are blameless.

familiar.text: And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.

modern.text: Additionally, they must first be tested. Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons.

original.text: καὶ οὗτοι δὲ δοκιμαζέσθωσαν πρῶτον, εἶτα διακονείτωσαν ἀνέγκλητοι ὄντες.

verses.restored: Women likewise, dignified, not slanderous, sober, trustworthy in all things.

familiar.text: Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.

modern.text: In the same way, the women must be dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things.

original.text: γυναῖκας ὡσαύτως σεμνάς, μὴ διαβόλους, νηφαλίους, πιστὰς ἐν πᾶσιν.

verses.restored: Let servants/deacons be husbands of one wife, leading children and their own households beautifully/well.

familiar.text: Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.

modern.text: A deacon must be the husband of but one wife, a good manager of his children and of his own household.

original.text: διάκονοι ἔστωσαν μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρες, τέκνων καλῶς προϊστάμενοι καὶ τῶν ἰδίων οἴκων·

verses.restored: For those who have served beautifully/well acquire a beautiful/good standing for themselves and much boldness in trust that is in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.

modern.text: For those who have served well as deacons acquire for themselves a high standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus. The Mystery of Godliness

original.text: οἱ γὰρ καλῶς διακονήσαντες βαθμὸν ἑαυτοῖς καλὸν περιποιοῦνται καὶ πολλὴν παρρησίαν ἐν πίστει τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: These things I write to you, hoping to come to you soon,

familiar.text: These things write I unto thee, hoping to come unto thee shortly:

modern.text: Although I hope to come to you soon, I am writing you these things

original.text: Ταῦτά σοι γράφω, ἐλπίζων ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ⸂ἐν τάχει⸃,

verses.restored: but if I delay, so that you may know how it is necessary to conduct oneself in the household of the Divine, which is assembly of living Divine, pillar and support of the truth.

familiar.text: But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.

modern.text: in case I am delayed, so that you will know how each one must conduct himself in God’s household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ βραδύνω, ἵνα εἰδῇς πῶς δεῖ ἐν οἴκῳ θεοῦ ἀναστρέφεσθαι, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐκκλησία θεοῦ ζῶντος, στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς ἀληθείας·

verses.restored: And confessedly great is the mystery of reverence/godliness: Who was manifested in flesh, made righteous/justified in Spirit, seen by messengers, proclaimed among nations, trusted in world, taken up in glory.

familiar.text: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.

modern.text: By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory.

original.text: καὶ ὁμολογουμένως μέγα ἐστὶν τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας μυστήριον· ⸀Ὃς ἐφανερώθη ἐν σαρκί, ἐδικαιώθη ἐν πνεύματι, ὤφθη ἀγγέλοις, ἐκηρύχθη ἐν ἔθνεσιν, ἐπιστεύθη ἐν κόσμῳ, ἀνελήμφθη ἐν δόξῃ.

translation_notes: Episkope is oversight and episkopos overseer; the emphasis is character and care, not status hierarchy.
Diakonoi is servants/deacons. Verse 11 may refer to women deacons or wives; ambiguity is preserved as women likewise.
Mystery of godliness in 3:16 is likely hymnic/confessional; manifested in flesh is preserved without over-specifying textual variants in this first pass.
